text:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: prod-gpu-1 pool reporting capacity exhaustion and autoscaler errors. Queue depth > 18k, enqueue rate spike 3x. Multiple nodes flapping due to CUDA/Xid errors. Pager routed to #incidents at 2245078901

ajay: I'm on it — paging SRE rotation. seeing a steady increase in `queued_requests` since 10:12 UTC. autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts failing with node registration timeouts.

maria: Any customer impact known? CX noticing increased 5xxs on inference endpoints.

kevin: Runtime reports a bunch of `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` / Xid 31 and 69. suspect driver/firmware regression on the latest node image.

sophie: Autoscaler is hitting the 20-node pool cap for prod-gpu-1, but even when nodes come up they fail to register with the driver agent.

ajay: Short plan: 1) throttle new request ingress to reduce queue growth 2) route critical customers to warm-dedicated pool 3) stop autoscaler from launching more nodes until we confirm driver health 4) start remediation on flapped nodes.

kevin: Agreed. I'm grabbing runtime logs and will paste relevant tails.

kevin: ```
[driver] 2026-03-15T10:15:02Z ERROR gpu0: Xid 31: GPU HANG detected
[driver] 2026-03-15T10:15:03Z WARN node-agent: failing healthcheck, deregistering node
[runtime] 2026-03-15T10:15:04Z ERROR oom: worker process killed by OOM
```

dave: @ajay I can start the customer failover script to redirect traffic for top 10 customers to warm-dedicated. Need sign-off.

ajay: Please do. Prioritize per the active SLAs list. Maria, can you coordinate with CS/AE for the impacted accounts?

maria: On it. I'll open a short blast for top 5 and a targeted note for the rest. ETA 10m.

ingrid: Ops note — temporarily raising per-tenant rate limit to 50% of normal for non-SLA tiers to protect capacity. Applied token bucket policy on API gateway.

ops-bot: config-change: rate-limit updated for /v1/completions -> tier:standard -> 50% (applied by ingrid)

kevin: I'm seeing a recurring pattern: nodes boot, drivers load, a small subset of long-running kernels trigger a memory leak that cascades to OOM and Xid. That effectively removes capacity faster than autoscaler can replenish.

ajay: So autoscaler is oscillating: it sees capacity drop -> starts nodes -> nodes fail under runtime faults -> autoscaler hits retry limit -> gives up -> queue grows.

sophie: I can temporarily disable scale-down and bump the pool cap for prod-gpu-1 while we triage, but need approval due to cost.

maria: Approve for 2 hours. Customer impact is material; better to stabilize.

ajay: Do it. Also set manual scaling to +10 nodes and pause automated replacements.

sophie: Done. Manual cap +10 applied, autoscaler replacement paused. ops-bot confirms.

ops-bot: pool-update: prod-gpu-1 cap increased +10, autoscaler replace disabled (applied by sophie)

kevin: For immediate mitigation, we'll: 1) evict suspected job classes that trigger long-lived kernels to a quarantine node group 2) enable aggressive prefix/KV cache eviction to free memory 3) roll driver to last-known-good on a small canary.

ajay: Who can run the evict script? dave?

dave: Running now. Script output: `evicted 142 jobs from long-run queue; moved 98 to quarantine-group`

kevin: Initiating canary driver rollback on 2 nodes in prod-gpu-1-canary. Monitoring register and runtime self-checks.

kevin: Canary logs look clean so far (0 Xid in 3m, driver health ok). Rolling to 6 more nodes.

ingrid: Monitoring dashboards: queue depth dropped from 18.3k -> 7.6k after throttles + evictions. Token spend down ~30%.

maria: Customer update draft: "We're mitigating a GPU pool capacity incident affecting inference latency and errors. We've routed top SLA customers to capacity pools and implemented throttles. Engineers are rolling a driver rollback and expect stabilization within 1 hour." OK to send?

ajay: Send it. Add contact for urgent cases.

customer-success: Sent to top 10 customers. Two customers reported degraded throughput but no data loss. AEs notified.

kevin: Rolling driver rollback to remaining nodes. Still seeing a tiny fraction of nodes fail to recover — those nodes show repeated `proc|oom` traces in syslog. We'll cordon and reprovision if they don't pass health checks.

ajay: I'm going to publish a short incident note in #incidents once we reach steady state. Please keep adding logs and timelines here.

dave: Manual reprovision completed on 4 nodes; they came back healthy.

kevin: Post-rollback metrics: Xid occurrences down 98%, node flaps stopped, effective serving capacity recovered to ~85% of baseline. Autoscaler still paused.

sophie: Given recovery, I'm going to unpause autoscaler but keep replacement paused for another 30m. Also lowering manual cap back to +5.

ops-bot: autoscaler: unpaused (scale-up allowed), replacement still disabled; pool cap set to +5 (applied by sophie)

ingrid: Queue trending down to 1.2k. Latency P95 trending toward normal. No new 5xx spikes in last 6m.

ajay: Great work. Next actions: - postmortem runbook (kevin+dave) - verify driver image and revert pipeline approval (kevin+eng-runtime) - follow-up customer comms with RCA draft (maria+cs) - schedule upgrade window for proper driver fix (product + eng)

maria: Will coordinate customer RCA and SLA credits as needed.

kevin: Captured all relevant artifacts: driver logs, node syslogs, runtime traces, autoscaler event history. Uploading to /mnt/incidents/2245078901/artifacts.tar.gz now.

ajay: Handoff to next oncall at 2245082400. If anything regresses, re-pager. Otherwise we'll de-escalate and start the RCA.

incident-bot: oncall-handoff: ajay -> dave at 2245082400.

dave: Acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor overnight and pick up the RCA tasks tomorrow morning.

maria: Closing customer loop for now. Will reopen if new reports come in.

kevin: Quick note for postmortem: root cause suspected at interaction between new driver memory allocator change + long-lived kernel patterns -> leak leading to OOM -> Xid. Autoscaler retries amplified the effect by cycling failing nodes.

ajay: Thanks team. Incident contained; follow-up items assigned. :tada:
